meta.title: ANATOMICA reproductive system clinical records — Milestone 14

sources.S1: TeachMeAnatomy — The Testes and Epididymis (teachmeanatomy.info): scrotal position and posterolateral epididymis, descent through the inguinal canal, lobules of Sertoli-lined seminiferous tubules, Leydig-cell testosterone, tunica vaginalis and albuginea, rete testis and efferent tubules, epididymal head/body/tail as one coiled duct, testicular arteries from the abdominal aorta with cremasteric and ductal anastomoses, pampiniform plexus to the testicular veins (left to the left renal vein, right to the IVC), lumbar lymphatics, testicular plexus innervation
sources.S2: TeachMeAnatomy — The Prostate Gland (teachmeanatomy.info): largest accessory gland, walnut-sized, two-thirds glandular and one-third fibromuscular, position at the bladder neck, McNeal zones (central ~25%, transitional 5–10%, peripheral ~65%, anterior fibromuscular stroma), prostatic ducts into the prostatic urethra, prostatic arteries mainly from the internal iliac, prostatic plexus to the internal iliac veins with the Batson communication, inferior hypogastric innervation, flanking neurovascular bundles
sources.S3: SEER Training Modules (U.S. National Cancer Institute) — Duct System (training.seer.cancer.gov): duct order testes -> epididymis -> ductus deferens -> ejaculatory duct -> urethra; epididymis a ~6 m coiled tube maturing and storing sperm; the ductus deferens' course and ampulla; spermatic cord contents; ejaculatory duct formation and emptying; the urethra's three regions and shared urinary/reproductive role
sources.S4: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, §27.1 (read in the LibreTexts Human Anatomy ch. 23.2 mirror, med.libretexts.org): scrotum and its muscles, testes 4–5 cm with 300–400 lobules, straight tubules -> rete testes -> 15–20 efferent ductules, epididymis ~6 m / ~12-day transit, semen composition (sperm ~5%, seminal vesicles ~60%), prostatic citrate, PSA and seminalplasmin, bulbourethral mucus, the ductal system and vasectomy, the penis' erectile columns, glans and prepuce, erection by NO-mediated vasocongestion
sources.S5: TeachMeAnatomy — The Ovaries (teachmeanatomy.info): paired ovals on the posterior broad ligament via the mesovarium, hilum, oocyte and oestrogen/progesterone production, surface/cortex/medulla, suspensory and ovarian ligaments, ovarian arteries from the aorta with uterine contribution, asymmetric ovarian veins, ovarian and uterine plexus innervation, para-aortic lymphatics
sources.S6: TeachMeAnatomy — The Uterus (teachmeanatomy.info): fundus/body/cervix, anteversion and anteflexion, relations to bladder and rectum, perimetrium/myometrium/endometrium with the endometrial strata, broad, round, ovarian, cardinal and uterosacral ligaments, uterine artery from the internal iliac crossing the ureter, uterine venous plexus, iliac/sacral/aortic/inguinal lymphatics, uterovaginal plexus innervation
sources.S7: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, §27.2 (LibreTexts mirrors, consulted at chapter/excerpt level): ovaries as paired 2–3 cm ovals on the mesovarium, uterus ~5 cm wide by ~7 cm long with three parts and three wall layers, uterine tubes with distal fimbriae, vagina a ~10 cm muscular canal with its fornix at the cervix, vulva including the mons pubis as the pad of fat over the pubic bone, labia, clitoris, vestibule and Bartholin's glands
sources.S8: TeachMeAnatomy — The Perineum (teachmeanatomy.info; article text consulted in full extract): diamond region at the pelvic outlet, anatomical and surface borders, the transverse ischial line dividing urogenital and anal triangles, anal triangle contents (anal aperture, external anal sphincter, ischioanal fossae), the perineal body at the junction
sources.S9: InnerBody — Female Reproductive Organs of the Lower Torso (innerbody.com; excerpt level): vulva as the collective external organs, labia majora and minora, vagina connecting vulva to cervix, uterus between vagina and tubes, tubes extending toward the ovaries, the tract as a conduit for sperm and for birth
sources.S10: ANATOMICA project datasets consulted in-session: this milestone's BP3D 4.0 census (tools/repro_map.py), the cardiovascular module inventory (Milestone 5), the urinary module (Milestone 12), the endocrine inventory (Milestone 13) and the muscular module geometry (Milestone 4) — dataset facts and cross-module pointers only

meta.sourcing_rule: every field value is drawn only from the sources listed, consulted in this session, and cites them per field in the record's sources map; a field no consulted source supports is null and carries a verify entry naming it. TA names are not asserted anywhere in this tranche (no TA2 list consulted). Seven records link geometry the release carries (testis, epididymis, seminal vesicles, prostate, penis — assembled from its erectile parts — mons pubis, and the perineum with its anal part); the remaining nine link none — eight with the dataset absence recorded (the ductus deferens, the bulbourethral glands, and the female tract's pathway, ovary, uterine tube, uterus, vagina and vulva) and the male pathway with its own no-geometry statement. The urethra is not duplicated: the male pathway record states its relationship and points at the urinary module's records, and the checker resolves the pointer.

records.name: Male reproductive pathway
verify: the pathway record links no geometry itself: its stations' geometry is held by this module's organ records where the release carries them (testis, epididymis, seminal vesicles, prostate, erectile tissues), and the ductus deferens and ejaculatory duct stations have no BP3D 4.0 concept at all (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/repro_map.py)

records.note: The pathway crosses two module boundaries by design: it begins in this module's gonad and ends in the urinary module's urethra, and two of its stations are dataset absences carried as sourced text.
records.description: The route sperm take from production to exit. Formed in the seminiferous tubules of the testis, sperm leave the testis through the efferent ductules for the epididymis, and at ejaculation are driven along the ductus deferens, through the ejaculatory duct and out through the urethra — after they leave the testes, the sperm passes through the epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, and urethra (S3, S4).
records.urethra_relationship: The pathway's terminal segment is the urethra — a structure this module does not own. The release carries exactly one urethra concept (FMA19667), unsexed and undivided, and the urinary module (Milestone 12) holds it as its inventory record 'urethra', with clinical record structure.urethra: the urethra is the shared terminal channel of the urinary and male reproductive systems, running from the bladder to the external urethral orifice at the tip of the penis, a passageway for sperm and reproductive fluids and for urine — though never both at once, sphincters contracting to keep urine out of it while reproductive fluids pass (S3). It is censused there and cross-referenced here, never duplicated; its three regions (prostatic, membranous, spongy) exist in this module only as the pathway's sourced text, there being no regional urethra concepts in the release (S3, S4, S10).
records.glands_in_order: In the order their secretions join the stream: the seminal vesicles first, their duct joining the ductus deferens at its ampulla to form the ejaculatory duct, so their fluid enters with the sperm (S3, S4); the prostate next, its ducts opening into the prostatic urethra as the fluid passes (S2, S3); the bulbourethral glands last into the penile urethra — in fact discharged before the semen itself, as the pre-ejaculate (S3, S4).
records.semen_composition: Sperm make up only about 5 percent of the final volume of semen; the seminal vesicles contribute approximately 60 percent, the prostate and the bulbourethral glands most of the remainder (S4).
records.clinical_note: Vasectomy interrupts the pathway at its most accessible station: the ductus deferens is cut and sealed inside the scrotum, where it is bundled in the spermatic cord — clinicians regard the procedure as permanent (S4). The station is one the dataset does not carry at all.

records.name: Testis
verify: ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The male gonad is the dataset's best-served reproductive organ: geometry, its arteries and veins in the cardiovascular module, and this record — against the female gonad's sourced text over a total dataset absence (organ.ovary).
records.description: The male gonads: paired ellipsoid organs housed within the scrotum, each suspended by the spermatic cord, the epididymis applied to the posterolateral surface of each, and the left testis usually sitting lower than the right (S1).
records.parts: Each testis is divided by septa of its dense fibrous capsule, the tunica albuginea, into lobules of seminiferous tubules — OpenStax counts 300 to 400 lobules (S4) — where sperm develop, surrounded by sustentacular (Sertoli) cells, with the interstitial (Leydig) cells between the tubules producing testosterone (S1, S4). Formed sperm pass from the tubules into the straight tubules, then the rete testis, and leave through the efferent ductules (S4). Over the capsule lies the tunica vaginalis, a serous peritoneal sac covering the front and sides (S1, S4). No part, covering or tubule has a concept in the release — the data carries the organs as undivided volumes.
records.function: Spermatogenesis and androgen production: the testes produce sperm and androgens — principally testosterone, the hormone that supports male reproductive physiology — and are active throughout the reproductive lifespan (S1, S4).
records.dimension: Each testis is approximately 4 to 5 cm in length (S4). Sperm production proceeds more efficiently at 2 to 4 °C below core body temperature, which the scrotal position provides (S4).
records.arterial_supply: The paired testicular arteries arise from the abdominal aorta and descend through the inguinal canal in the spermatic cord — the route of the testis' own descent from the posterior abdominal wall; the cremasteric artery (from the inferior epigastric) and the artery of the ductus deferens (from the inferior vesical) anastomose with them (S1). The cardiovascular module carries both as records artery.right-testicular-artery and artery.left-testicular-artery, resolved by the checker (S10).
records.venous_drainage: The pampiniform plexus drains into the testicular veins, asymmetrically: the left testicular vein ends in the left renal vein, the right directly in the inferior vena cava (S1). Carried by the cardiovascular module as vein.right-testicular-vein and vein.left-testicular-vein (S10).
records.lymphatic_drainage: To the lumbar (para-aortic) lymph nodes, following the gonadal vessels back to their origin — not to the inguinal nodes, which drain the scrotal skin instead (S1). No lumbar node exists as a concept in the release (lymphatic module census), so this drainage is sourced text only.
records.innervation: Via the testicular plexus, derived from the renal and aortic plexuses (S1). No testicular nerve concept exists in the release (nervous module census), so this is sourced text only.
records.relations: Within the scrotum behind the penis, one testis per compartment of the scrotal septum (S4); the epididymis sits posterolateral (S1). Each testis reached the scrotum by descending from the posterior abdominal wall through the inguinal canal during development, carrying its vessels, nerves and lymphatics with it (S1).

records.name: Epididymis
verify: arterial_supply: no value asserted — none of the sources consulted in this session states the epididymis' own arterial supply in citable form (the testicular arteries are recorded on organ.testis); the field stays null rather than unsourced
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The only duct of the male pathway the release carries — the pathway is continuous in the data from the testis to here, and broken from here on.
records.description: A long, tightly coiled tube forming a comma-shaped organ along the superior and posterior margins of the testis — a single heavily coiled duct, not a bundle of ducts (S1, S3).
records.parts: Head, body and tail. The head is formed by the efferent ductules arriving from the rete testis; the body is the coiled duct itself; the tail is where mature sperm are stored and where the ductus deferens begins (S1, S3).
records.function: Maturation and storage: sperm leave the testis immature and incapable of fertilising an ovum, complete their maturation as they move through the epididymis, and are stored, fertile, in its tail until ejaculation (S3, S4).
records.dimension: About 6 metres long if straightened (S3, S4); sperm take an average of about 12 days to transit its coils (S4).
records.relations: Applied to the superior and posterior margins of the testis within the scrotum, continuous at its tail with the ductus deferens (S3).

ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: Sourced-text record for the pathway's missing middle: the duct a vasectomy interrupts has no more presence in the dataset than the ovary does.
records.description: A fibromuscular tube continuous with the tail of the epididymis, conducting sperm from the scrotum to the ejaculatory duct (S3, S4).
records.course: It begins at the tail of the epididymis and turns sharply upward along the posterior margin of the testis; bundled in the spermatic cord, it enters the abdominopelvic cavity through the inguinal canal, passes along the lateral pelvic wall, crosses over the ureter and the posterior portion of the urinary bladder, and descends behind the bladder toward the prostate, enlarging into the ampulla just before it reaches the gland (S3, S4).
records.function: Transport and proximal storage: sperm are stored in its proximal portion near the epididymis, and peristaltic contraction propels them through it at ejaculation (S3).
records.parts: Its named dilation is the ampulla, the flask-like enlargement just before the prostate, where it joins the duct of the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct (S3, S4). The spermatic cord that carries its proximal portion also contains the testicular artery and veins, lymphatics, the testicular nerve and the cremaster muscle (S3).
records.clinical_note: Because the duct is physically accessible within the scrotum, surgical sterilisation — vasectomy — cuts and seals a small section of it; the procedure is considered permanent (S4).

records.name: Seminal vesicles
verify: arterial_supply: no value asserted — none of the sources consulted in this session states the seminal vesicles' arterial supply in citable form; the field stays null rather than unsourced
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: Geometry-linked, unlike the duct they join: the release carries the glands but not the ductus deferens or the ejaculatory duct they complete.
records.description: Paired glands whose ducts join the ampullae of the ductus deferens behind the bladder to form the ejaculatory ducts, which then pass through the prostate and empty into the urethra (S3, S4).
records.function: Their secretion contributes approximately 60 percent of semen volume: rich in fructose, which the sperm's mitochondria burn for the ATP of movement, and alkaline, neutralising the acidic environment of the vagina; its prostaglandins act on the cervix (S4). Sperm are immobile until mixed with the seminal glands' secretions (S4).
records.relations: Posterior to the urinary bladder, the ductus deferens arched over it to meet them (S4); the ejaculatory ducts they form traverse the prostate gland (S3).

records.name: Prostate gland
verify: lymphatic_drainage: no value asserted — none of the sources consulted in this session states the prostate's lymphatic drainage in citable form; the field stays null rather than unsourced
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The release's only genital-system member gets the tranche's fullest gland record — geometry, zones, relations and the nerve-sparing relation included.
records.description: The largest accessory gland of the male reproductive system: a walnut-sized gland of muscular and glandular tissue — about two-thirds glandular, one-third fibromuscular — surrounding the prostatic urethra at the base of the urinary bladder (S2, S4). It is the one member the release files under its own genital system.
records.parts: McNeal's zones (S2): the central zone, about 25 percent, surrounds the ejaculatory ducts; the transitional zone, 5–10 percent, surrounds the urethra and is where benign prostatic hyperplasia arises; the peripheral zone, about 65 percent, is the posterior main body — the zone palpable on rectal examination; and the anterior fibromuscular stroma is the fourth zone. The traditional lobes are also described by the source (S2). The release carries the gland as one undivided concept: no zone or lobe exists in the data.
records.function: It excretes a milky fluid into the passing semen: proteolytic enzymes via prostatic ducts opening into the prostatic urethra — among them prostate-specific antigen (PSA), which liquefies semen after its initial coagulation — with citric acid and the antibiotic seminalplasmin (S2, S4).
records.relations: Inferior to the neck of the bladder, superior to the external urethral sphincter, levator ani inferolaterally, and the ampulla of the rectum posteriorly — the relation by which the peripheral zone is palpated on digital rectal examination (S2). Its thin fibrous capsule is adventitia-like, not a true capsule (S2).
records.arterial_supply: Prostatic arteries arising mainly from the internal iliac artery, with contributions from the internal pudendal and middle rectal arteries (S2).
records.venous_drainage: The prostatic venous plexus drains into the internal iliac veins, and communicates with the internal vertebral venous plexus (Batson's) (S2).
records.innervation: From the inferior hypogastric plexus (S2). The neurovascular bundles flank the gland on their way to the corpora cavernosa — the anatomical basis of nerve-sparing prostatectomy (S2).

records.note: The third accessory gland completes the pathway's gland order as sourced text; the release carries its two companions but not it.
records.description: Two small glands whose ducts open into the penile (spongy) urethra (S3, S4).
records.function: They release a thick, salty mucus that lubricates the end of the urethra and the vagina and cleans urine residues from the penile urethra; the fluid is released after arousal and shortly before the semen — the pre-ejaculate — and can pick up sperm already present in the urethra (S4).

records.name: Penis
verify: innervation: no value asserted — none of the sources consulted in this session states the penile innervation in citable form; the pudendal nerve is not asserted here, and no penile nerve concept exists in the release (nervous module census)
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: An organ the dataset represents only in pieces: three erectile structures here, five vessels in the cardiovascular module, and no whole-organ concept anywhere.
records.description: The male organ of copulation, delivering sperm into the female reproductive tract: flaccid for non-sexual actions such as urination, turgid and rod-like with sexual arousal (S4). The release has no penis concept — no concept is named 'penis' (exact-name probe-verified) — so this record is assembled from the three erectile structures the release does carry, with its vessels in the cardiovascular module (S10).
records.parts: The shaft is composed of three column-like chambers of erectile tissue: the two larger lateral corpora cavernosa, which together make up the bulk of the penis, and the smaller corpus spongiosum, felt as a raised ridge on the erect penis, which surrounds the spongy (penile) urethra (S4). The end of the penis is the glans penis, its skin rich in nerve endings; the skin of the shaft extends over the glans as a collar, the prepuce (foreskin) (S4). The prepuce has no concept in the release — 'prepuce' scores zero hits — and is text here only.
records.function: Copulation and semen delivery, and — through the spongy urethra it encloses — the exit of urine (S4). Erection is vasocongestion: on arousal, nitric oxide from nerve endings relaxes the smooth muscle of the penile arteries, the erectile chambers fill faster than the veins drain them, and the pressure of the filled chambers compresses the thin-walled venules, trapping the blood (S4).
records.arterial_supply: The penile arteries whose dilation drives erection (S4) are carried by name in the release only in the cardiovascular module: the dorsal arteries of the penis, records artery.right-dorsal-artery-of-penis and artery.left-dorsal-artery-of-penis (S10).
records.venous_drainage: The veins the release names for this organ are the cardiovascular module's records vein.deep-dorsal-vein-of-penis, vein.right-superficial-dorsal-vein-of-penis and vein.left-superficial-dorsal-vein-of-penis (S10); the erectile mechanism compresses the penile venules against drainage (S4).

records.name: Female reproductive pathway
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/repro_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry — for every station of the pathway, not one structure: 'ovary', 'uterus', 'vagina' and 'uterine' all score zero hits in both parts lists and in all six release tables
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: A pathway with no geometry at any station — the exact inverse of the male pathway, whose first stations are the dataset's best-served organs.
records.description: The route of the oocyte, and in pregnancy of the conceptus: the ovary produces and releases the oocyte, the uterine tube conveys it to the uterus, the uterus receives it — the usual site of implantation — and the vagina is the tract's canal to the exterior (S5, S6, S9).
records.function: Gamete production in the ovary, transport along the tube, implantation and gestation in the uterus, and delivery through the vagina: the internal organs work together as a conduit for sperm to reach the egg and for the development and birth of the fetus (S9).
records.dataset_note: Every station of this pathway is a dataset absence: not one of these structures has a concept in BP3D 4.0 (probe-verified per sex line by tools/repro_map.py). The pathway record exists so that the module states the female tract's sourced anatomy and its total absence in one place; the only female geometry in the module is the mons pubis, which is not a station of this pathway but the surface landmark at its end (structure.mons-pubis).

ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: The module's headline record: a fully sourced account (tier A on fields) of the female gonad over a total dataset absence — the mirror image of organ.testis, which has geometry, vessels and a census line.
records.description: The female gonads: paired, oval organs attached to the posterior surface of the broad ligament of the uterus by the mesovarium, a fold of peritoneum continuous with the ovaries' outer surface, with neurovascular structures entering at the hilum (S5).
records.parts: Three histological components (S5): the surface, a simple cuboidal epithelium (the germinal epithelium) over a dense connective-tissue capsule; the cortex, a connective-tissue stroma carrying numerous ovarian follicles, each an oocyte surrounded by follicular cells; and the medulla, loose connective tissue with a rich neurovascular network entering at the hilum. No component has a concept in the release.
records.function: To produce oocytes (female gametes) in preparation for fertilisation, and to produce the sex steroid hormones oestrogen and progesterone in response to the pituitary gonadotrophins LH and FSH (S5).
records.dimension: Paired ovals some 2 to 3 cm long, seated in the pelvic cavity: the gonads develop in the mesonephric ridge and descend through the abdomen, but unlike the testes the ovaries stop in the pelvis (S5, S7).
records.ligaments: Two peritoneal ligaments (S5): the suspensory ligament of the ovary, extending from the mesovarium to the pelvic wall and containing the neurovascular structures; and the ligament of the ovary, extending from the ovary to the fundus of the uterus, then continuing from the uterus to the labium majus as the round ligament of the uterus.
records.arterial_supply: The paired ovarian arteries arise directly from the abdominal aorta, inferior to the renal arteries; there is also a contribution from the uterine arteries (S5). Dataset gap, recorded: the cardiovascular module carries no ovarian artery record, the release having no ovarian vessel concept either (S10) — unlike the testis, whose arteries the sister module holds, this supply has no cross-module pointer to resolve.
records.venous_drainage: Paired ovarian veins: the left drains into the left renal vein, the right directly into the inferior vena cava (S5) — the same asymmetry as the testicular veins, and likewise without a cardiovascular record in the release (S10).
records.lymphatic_drainage: Lymph from the ovaries drains into the para-aortic nodes (S5). No para-aortic node exists as a concept in the release (lymphatic module census).
records.innervation: Sympathetic and parasympathetic fibres from the ovarian and uterine (pelvic) plexuses respectively, reaching the ovary via the suspensory ligament to enter at the hilum (S5).

records.note: Sourced-text record; the fimbriae are its one sourced part, the rest of the tube's regional anatomy flagged rather than filled.
records.description: Paired tubes extending laterally from the upper uterus toward the ovaries, serving as the pathway for oocytes from the ovary to the uterine cavity (S7, S9).
records.parts: The distal end, nearest the ovary, carries finger-like projections — the fimbriae — which overhang the ovary and receive the released oocyte (S7).
records.function: Transport: the tube conveys the oocyte, and after fertilisation the embryo, slowly to the uterus, where implantation follows (S7, S9).

records.name: Uterus
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/repro_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry — 'uterus' and 'uterine' score zero hits in both parts lists and in all six release tables, and the wall layers with them: 'endometrium', 'myometrium' and 'perimetrium' are likewise zero-hit probes
ta_name: not asserted — no TA2 term list was consulted in this session
records.note: Fully sourced (tier A on fields) over a total dataset absence, like organ.ovary: the release contains the ureter this organ's artery crosses, but not the organ.
records.description: A thick-walled muscular organ of the female reproductive tract, capable of expansion to accommodate a growing fetus, connected distally to the vagina and laterally to the uterine tubes (S6). It is a secondary sex organ — a component of the tract that matures during puberty under the influence of the ovaries' sex hormones (S6).
records.parts: Three parts (S6): the fundus, the top of the uterus above the entry point of the uterine tubes; the body, the usual site for implantation of the blastocyst; and the cervix, the lower part linking the uterus with the vagina, structurally and functionally different to the rest of the uterus.
records.function: The maintenance and transportation of gametes (S6), the housing of the implanted conceptus through gestation, and — by the contractions of its myometrium — delivery (S6, S9).
records.wall_layers: The fundus and body are composed of three tissue layers (S6): the perimetrium, a double-layered peritoneal membrane; the myometrium, a thick smooth-muscle layer whose cells undergo hypertrophy and hyperplasia during pregnancy; and the endometrium, the inner mucous membrane, whose deep stratum basalis changes little through the cycle and is not shed, while its superficial stratum functionalis proliferates under oestrogen, becomes secretory under progesterone, and is shed at menstruation. No layer has a concept in the release.
records.dimension: About 5 cm wide and 7 cm long in the non-pregnant adult (S7).
records.position: In the normal adult the uterus is anteverted with respect to the vagina and anteflexed with respect to the cervix, lying immediately posterosuperior to the bladder and anterior to the rectum; its exact location varies with the distension of the bladder (S6).
records.ligaments: The tone of the pelvic floor is the primary support; the ligaments secure it further (S6): the broad ligament, a double layer of peritoneum attaching the sides of the uterus to the pelvis and acting as its mesentery; the round ligament, a gubernacular remnant running from the uterine horns to the labia majora via the inguinal canal, maintaining anteversion; the ovarian ligament, joining the ovaries to the uterus; the cardinal ligament at the base of the broad ligament, from the cervix to the lateral pelvic walls, containing the uterine artery and vein; and the uterosacral ligament, from the cervix to the sacrum. No ligament has a concept in the release.
records.arterial_supply: The uterine artery, a branch of the internal iliac artery (S6). It crosses the ureter approximately 1 cm lateral to the internal os — 'water under the bridge' — the relation that hysterectomy must respect (S6).
records.venous_drainage: Via a plexus in the broad ligament that drains into the uterine veins (S6).
records.lymphatic_drainage: Via the iliac, sacral, aortic and inguinal lymph nodes (S6). None exists as a concept in the release (lymphatic module census).
records.innervation: Sympathetic fibres from the uterovaginal plexus — largely the anterior and intermediate parts of the inferior hypogastric plexus; parasympathetic fibres from the pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2–S4); the cervix largely by the inferior fibres of the uterovaginal plexus; afferents ascending through the inferior hypogastric plexus to T10–T12 and L1 (S6).

records.note: Shared ground in every sense: one region for both sex lines, its clinical anatomy sourced whole, its geometry borrowed entire from a muscle another module owns.
records.description: An anatomical region in the pelvis, located between the thighs, representing the most inferior part of the pelvic outlet and separated from the pelvic cavity superiorly by the pelvic floor (S8). In clinical usage the word is often narrowed to the area between the external genitalia and the anus; anatomically it is the whole diamond (S8).
records.boundaries: Anatomical borders (S8): anteriorly the pubic symphysis; posteriorly the tip of the coccyx; laterally the inferior pubic rami and inferior ischial rami and the sacrotuberous ligament; the roof is the pelvic floor and the base skin and fascia. Surface borders, with the limbs abducted (S8): anteriorly the mons pubis in females, the base of the penis in males; laterally the medial surfaces of the thighs; posteriorly the superior end of the intergluteal cleft.
records.parts: A theoretical line drawn transversely between the ischial tuberosities divides the diamond into the anterior urogenital triangle and the posterior anal triangle (S8). The anal triangle — bounded by the coccyx, the sacrotuberous ligaments and the intertuberosity line — contains the anal aperture, the external anal sphincter muscle and the paired ischioanal fossae (S8). The urogenital triangle is associated with the structures of the urogenital system, the external genitalia and the urethra (S8). At the junction of the two triangles sits the perineal body, an irregular fibromuscular mass at the central point of the perineum (S8). Of these named parts, none has a concept in the release: the triangles, the perineal body and the ischioanal fossae are all zero-hit shared-line probes (S10).
records.function: The region contains the structures that support the urogenital and gastrointestinal systems, and so plays its part in micturition, defecation, sexual intercourse and childbirth (S8).
records.dataset_note: The release's perineal geometry is a single muscle's shape: the perineum and its anal part carry the same four mesh files in PART-OF, and those four files are exactly the file set of the external anal sphincter — the muscular module's record muscle.external-anal-sphincter, censused in this module as a cross-reference (S10). The sphincter is the anal triangle's one muscular content the source names (S8) and the only perineal structure the dataset draws.
